title: Edge-index watcher holds the reindex publication guard on passes that do not rebuild, starving reindex admission
wanted_capability: bbox_reindex should be refused with EdgeIndexRebuildInProgress only while an edge-index rebuild parse or publication is actually running. The watcher currently takes the publication guard (index_writer.try_begin_edge_index_rebuild) at the top of every pass, before deciding whether to rebuild, and holds it through store-only nudge deferrals, searcher refreshes, authority capture, and health-record writes. Under a steady stream of store nudges the guard is held for most of wall-clock time, so reindex admission (which fails fast rather than waiting) keeps being refused after the last real rebuild finished. Wanted: acquire the guard only for passes that will rebuild (re-capturing authority under the guard), and report the holder's start time in the refusal so a long hold is visible.
missing_primitive: publication-guard scope limited to actual rebuilds, plus holder age in the EdgeIndexRebuildInProgress refusal
fallback_used: Daemon restart clears the latch (at the cost of restarting any in-flight schema rebuild, which is expensive).
evidence: src/server/routes.rs spawn_edge_index_rebuild_watcher: try_begin_edge_index_rebuild precedes should_rebuild_edge_index and the deferral and searcher-refresh branches
crates/bbox-indexing/src/index/writer_actor.rs EdgeIndexRebuildActivityGuard (RAII Drop release), reserve_reindex fails fast with IndexWriterRetryableError::EdgeIndexRebuildInProgress
notes: Triage trace: the guard has been an RAII Drop guard since before this gap was filed, so a set-without-release path is not the mechanism. The traced cause is guard scope: every watcher pass, including store-only nudge deferrals, holds it. Whether that alone explains the originally observed 10+ minute refusal window is not proven.
